utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Jadranko Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today is Wednesday. I'd like to greet the accused, the ladies and gentlemen in the court, the lawyers, Mr. Scott and his associate, as well as all the people assisting us in the courtroom. Just a housekeeping matter I would like to deal with, three oral decisions that I would like to read out. Before that, I had told you last year [as interpreted] that on Thursday, we would be sitting in the afternoon. It so happens that in the Seselj case, there is no witness for today, so we will be able to sit in the morning tomorrow, as had been initially planned. I hope this is not going to be a problem for anyone. Mr. Karnavas, no problem. Fine. We shall therefore sit in the morning tomorrow, as previously planned. We shall move into private session, because I have three decisions I'd like to hand down in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had a few housekeeping matters to deal with. I apologise for having made you wait. Mr. Karnavas, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President and Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom, and good morning, Mr. Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's pick up where we left off yesterday. We were talking about the Livno municipality. During the period that you were drafting all this legislation that we saw that came from the HVO HZ-HB, so with that introduction let's go to 1D 00314. This is a document dated 19 November 1992. 1D 00314. And we see this is a decision on the amount and manner of disbursement of salaries and fringe benefits in the Livno municipality. If you could comment very briefly on this.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this decision specifies the highest possible salary to be paid in the Municipality of Livno. The amount is 200 German marks. The exchange rate for Croatian dinar and the German mark is set in accordance with the median exchange rate set by the National Bank of Croatia, and the SDK is ordered to provide the exchange rate at the end of the month. All these elements are in contravention of the decisions and the decrees passed by the Croatian Defence Council of the HZ-HB. In Article 9, the HVO of the Livno municipality takes upon itself the power to exempt from paying taxes and contributions, some parties, and this is definitely not within the purview of the municipalities under any laws and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then if we look at the very last page of this decision as to where this decision was distributed, again we see, under number 5, it was distributed to the political parties HDZ and SDA, but do you see anywhere where your department would have been notified of this particular decision, or the HVO HZ-HB as an executive authority?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not notified about the decisions taken by the municipal HVOs. Many of them did not have their official gazettes. Article 12 states that this decision would be published in the Official Gazette of the Municipality of Livno, but it was first published in the end of 1993, early 1994, so it was not possible to learn what the municipalities were doing, except from complaints put in by companies and individuals who felt that the solutions put in place by the municipalities were much more detrimental to their operation than the regulations of the HVO HZ-HB. So we were thus able sporadically to learn what the municipalities were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's look at the next document, again Livno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Karnavas. This is an interesting point, Mr. Tomic. You said you received complaints. Was there any action upon these complaints? Were the complaints some sort of a legal or political remedy or was it just something that the "government" heard, but not something that was of any character that prompted action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, in the sphere of finances, those who are in charge of implementing decisions were the municipal offices of the HVO, which were set up by the municipal HVOs. The complaints that we received came mostly from companies that had to pay additional levies that were not set by the HVO HZ-HB in its instruments. So this was not an administrative proceeding. Those were merely some complaints that we received, and then we would talk to the representatives of the municipal offices and tried to learn what this was all about. And then on the basis of the letters that we sent to the municipal HVOs, we warned them that the regulations of the HZ-HB were not being enforced. So it was not a complaint as part of administrative proceedings. It was simply a matter of people having to pay a lot of money and then coming to us to complain about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And when you wrote them a letter, did that have an effect or was it thrown into the waste paper basket, as it were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as you saw from the documents yesterday, there were many meetings, many letters, and there was no proper response because the presidents of the municipal HVOs were at the same time members of the Presidency of the HZ-HB, so they were our bosses, our superiors, and they felt that they could pass such decisions or at least postpone the time before they actually started implementing the decisions of the HVO HZ-HB. In some areas, it took quite a long time, up until well into 1994, for them to fully implement the regulations of the HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And sticking with this point a little bit, yesterday you indicated that it took you all the way up until, say, the end of 1993 for the financial police to be up and running. We saw the legislation come in, I believe, at the end of -- or towards the end of 1992, but it wasn't until 1993 that you indicated that it was up and running and functioning. Could you have used the financial police to force the presidents of the municipalities to comply with these -- you know, with the decisions or to overturn certain actions that were taken by the presidents of the municipalities or the municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The financial police started operating in early March 1993, after the first employees were hired, and in the first period it focused mostly on collecting taxes and contributions that the companies had not paid. At that time, there was -- it was not possible for the financial police to control the municipal HVOs. It only started happening in 1994, because it was simply not strong enough. And on the basis of their findings, the then finance minister again sent letters warning the House of Representatives of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna that the regulations of Herceg-Bosna -- that the sanctions could not be enforced against the municipal HVOs because of this overall attitude, which was the consequence of the fact that the presidents of the municipalities were at the same time members of the Presidency of the HZ-HB or later on of the House of Representatives of the Croatian republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, thank you. And also going back to the answer you gave with the previous document, let's look now at 1D 00272, and we can see there's an Official Gazette. It's dated February 1994. This is a decision on the temporary financing of the municipal HVO. And then if we look at Article 8 in this decision, we see "1 February 1993." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where it says "Number 01-023," and then we see "Livno, 16 February," is that 1993 or 1994 do we have in the Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This illustrates the fact that it was impossible for the decisions of the municipal HVOs to reach us at the time when they were passed. I mentioned a little while ago that the Official Gazette of the Livno municipality was first published in the end of 1993, early 1994. This is an issue from 1993-1994, and this is where a decision from February 1993 is published. So, officially, this decision and other decisions could not reach us until they were published in the Official Gazette. We could not have learnt about them before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what's wrong with this particular decision, if anything? I mean, to the naked eye, it looks pretty good, for those of us who are untrained.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see in Article 2 the municipal HVO orders the banks in Livno that every month, when pensions are remitted from abroad, that they should first pay 10 per cent of those transfers for the purposes of the defence to the finance office of the HVO in Livno and then to go on and to transfer the pensions to the accounts of those old-age pensioners if they show up at all. The decree stipulated that citizens had to pay the 10 per cent, but here the municipal HVO orders the bank to skim 10 per cent off the overall amount, regardless of whether an old-age pensioner would come in at all to collect the money.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And is this consistent with the legal instruments that your department had put in place?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is in contravention of the principles that were enshrined in our documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. 1D 00311, this is dated now 16 March 1993. This is a decision on minimum conditions for converting existing debts and credits. And could you give us a brief comment on this document and tell us whether this is in keeping with the HVO HZ-HB Department of Finance decisions or decrees?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the preamble this refers to the instruction on the production of the annual statement of accounts for 1992. It is a very complex document that requires a lot of expertise and it was supposed to resolve the issues for the period 1991 when we still had the Yugoslav dinar to take in -- into account the privatization, the war damage, this whole issue of currencies and the purpose was to find some economic modalities so that by the 1st of January, 1993 books could be kept by the companies properly and that they could simply continue with their business, and this decision rescinds this instruction that is actually referenced here and an option is put in place that all the liabilities and assets of the companies existing on the 31st of March should be converted from Yugoslav dinars into German marks based on the exchange rate of the National Bank of Yugoslavia, the exchange rate that was valid at that time, and that for the period of the 1st of April until the 31st of December, 1992 the conversion should be made based on the median exchange rate valid on the day of the exchange listed by the National Bank of Croatia, so this is in contravention of the instruction that was enacted by the HVO H-HB and in the actual fact, it favors the legal entities -- it puts the legal entities from Livno municipality in more favourable position in relation to others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, we'll pick up from 1D 00310. This is 26 March 1993, and this is a decision on financial contributions for the Livno --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas. Shouldn't we try to have the witness answer your last question again, because it is still completely unrecorded, his answer. If you look at the transcript, there's a jump now. There's your question on line 16 of page 14, and then it starts anew with your reference to document ID 00310, and in between the witness had given an answer which I think is interesting enough to figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. I assume -- I assume, and I'll be corrected from the gentleman or by the gentleman, that that will ultimately be put into the transcript, because it is being tape-recorded. THE REPORTER: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Excuse me for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't want to take up more time since this was being recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: No, absolutely fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Unless my colleagues need it right now on the record, but I think they can live without it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 00310, this is 26 March 1993, and this is a decision on financial contributions. If you could give us a very quick opinion on this.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Livno municipality was one of the municipalities with a large number of persons working abroad. Those people did not respond to the call-up, the mobilisation that was declared at one point in Livno, and this decision now imposes penalties on those conscripts, persons liable for military service. Those who did have visas that they had obtained before the 1st of October, 1991 had to pay 900 German marks until the time their visa expired, and then they had to report to their military unit in Livno. And in Article 2, it is stipulated that those who had fled to Germany, they are labelled here as illegal workers, as deserters. They were supposed to pay 900 German marks until the time when they come back, every month. So this decision is a decision that was a sup to the troops that were already in military units in Livno municipality, because they had complained about those who had left, who had gone abroad, or remained there, failing to respond to the call-up. The decision itself was -- could not be enforced, for technical reasons. This is a decision from the financial sphere, yet it is the Defence office of the municipal HVO in Livno was supposed to enforce it. It was placed within its jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I'm going to ask you to move a little bit quicker on these documents so we can -- 1D 00306. This is 3 May 1993. This is a decision on exemption of payment for contributions and taxes from personal incomes of mobilised workers in the Livno HVO units. And if you could tell us whether this is in keeping with the HVO HZ-HB legal instruments that were in place at the time.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in contravention of those regulations, because the municipal HVO could not exempt businesses from payment of taxes and contributions on salaries under the HZ-HB regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if we look at, very quickly, 1D 00304, would your answer be the same, that this is in contravention?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is again contrary to those regulations. This means that the area of the Livno municipality is isolated. According to this decision, wholesale companies can only sell their goods within the municipality, and other companies from outside of the municipality could not sell in the municipality itself. As a consequence, many of those companies moved out of the area of the municipality so that they could work in accordance with the regulations of the HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at 1D 00305. This is a decision on exemption from paying taxes and contributions of certain salaries. You can have a look at this. This is 8 May 1993.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, under the regulations of the HZ-HB, municipalities did not have the power to exempt any entities from payment of taxes and contributions. In this case, we're talking about the medical centre, the healthcare centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at 1D 00302, this is a decision on financing of the defence of Livno by individual farmers, cattle-breeders, and we see, for instance, under Roman numeral II 40 sheep, 50 cows, 30 goats, or 20 pigs for fattening. Can you please look at this decision and tell us what is this decision about? What is Livno doing here? This is 13 May 1993.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an atypical tax decision which shows how the municipality introduced new forms of taxation; in this case, people who owned cattle. But again we see here that there are people who were supposed to control all that, village commanders. This is theretofore unknown category in terms of financial control, so this was authored by the municipal HVO of Livno. It has nothing to do with the regulations of the HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 00275, this is a conclusion now, 6 July 1992.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, yet another exemption that the Livno municipality was not empowered to impose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 00295. This is a decision determining salaries of the village commanders. I take it that had to deal with those who are going to be monitoring the sheep and the cattle for taxation.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and I think the taxes collected in this manner could not even cover the salaries of the village commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look finally at 1D 00288, this is a conclusion on channeling the 1993 taxes and contributions into the budget of the Livno municipal HVO. This may be of interest in ending up this sort of vignette as far as what one municipality, Livno in particular, is doing at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I just ask a question of understanding regarding the previous document, yes, 1D 00295. Village commanders, "village," is that what was called "local community" in other -- the other day when I asked what "community" was? It was explained, local communities. Here we have the term "village." It's probably a matter of -- may be a matter of translation, also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The term was "commune," "commune."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It had been "commune," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is "village," so is it the same?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Local communities were a form of the organisation of local government below the level of municipalities, so there were local communities both in towns and in rural areas. Towns would have several local communities, each community being made up of several neighbourhoods, and in rural areas mostly each village would constitute a local community.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: So the term "village" is not the same as the term "local community." By "village," you mean a group of houses, irrespective of the political organisation or administrative organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you can give us a brief comment on 288 so we can move on.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I spoke about the putting together of the first budget of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna for 1994. Then the Ministry of Finance exerted pressure on the House of Representatives, and especially on the presidents of the municipal HVOs who were members of that House of Representatives, to enforce the regulations of Herceg-Bosna. The Livno municipality promised, as it were, to pay taxes and contributions on to the account of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna as of January 1st, 1994, but on January 15th they adopted a conclusion that the payment of taxes, of contributions pertaining to liabilities from 1993, shall be channeled to the accounts of the Livno municipality, even though, even in 1993, those monies belonged to the budget of HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Unless there are any questions on that, I'll move on. In order to save some time, we're going to skip the document pertaining to Siroki Brijeg, which are 1D 02519, 2523, 2524, and 2526. We'll also skip, for the sake of time, Capljina, which is 1D 01123 and 1D 01120. And we'll also skip Mostar, which is 1D 00635. I know you are prepared to discuss them as examples. So we'll just move on to now Orasje, this is one -- and Zupanja, which is one document and it's 1D 0 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a question for you. We've just reviewed a whole set of documents on the Livno municipality, but I'm sure there are other examples of this type for other municipalities as well. In those documents, we see that municipalities are taking decisions that are not in line with what had been decided at a higher level, basically at the level of the HZ-HB. Did you personally know that for Livno, for instance, such decisions were contrary to what you were planning to do in public accounting and in the financial and economic areas in Herceg-Bosna, because we've just seen that all those decisions were published in the Official Gazette in Livno. Were you personally aware of the fact that municipalities were making decisions that were not in line with what you had planned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was obvious, from monitoring the revenues of the budget of HZ-HB, we could see that in some municipalities the regulations of HZ-HB were not being respected. We reacted by contacting the finance offices of the municipal HVOs. They were municipal bodies, and they always replied that those were decisions of the municipal HVO. And when we spoke to the president of the municipal HVO, he would say that they must finance their defence and they would make use of their positions of members of the HZ-HB to implement their own decisions rather than those of the HZ-HB. The excuse was always that they had to pay for the defence, for healthcare, for pensioners, and that is why at the decisive point in time when the budget for 1994 was drafted, the budget took up a loan and directed the donations of the diaspora into the budget so the budget of the HZ-HB could take over all liabilities and make it impossible for the municipal HVOs to argue that they had to pay for those purposes, and thus they would no longer have an excuse for not respecting the regulations of HZ-HB. But here I'm talking about early 1994. Up until that time, the municipalities occasionally would act in contravention of our regulations and do whatever was good for them at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the municipalities did not abide by the regulations, I guess it was a major political issue. Did you speak to Mr. Prlic and to Mr. Boban about it, and if you did, what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was an experience not peculiar to the finance department. Other departments were faced with it too. On several occasions, as the HVO HZ-HB, we would direct such remarks to the municipal HVOs and the Presidency of the HZ-HB. Yesterday, we saw a letter that I sent because these situations were getting more frequent, especially after changes on the battlefield.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll get back to my question. The situation is clear. We can see that the municipalities and their leaders do not comply with the regulations, and you said a moment ago that it wasn't only in your municipality that the question arose. The question also arose in other municipalities. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In other departments, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, there is a major problem, politically speaking, because the municipalities are not applying the decisions taken by the HZ-HB. My question is a very simple one. In such a situation, did you inform, in writing or orally, Mr. Prlic and Mr. Boban? Did you tell them what the situation was like? And if you did, what did they say to you by way of a response, orally or in writing, to put an end to the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The departments informed the HVO HZ-HB and directly Mr. Boban. The HVO HZ-HB informed Mr. Boban also of its conclusions, and the Presidency of the HZ-HB, but the Presidency did not meet, or only very seldom, and we had no defined position or reply of the Presidency of the HZ-HB, which obviously avoided the discussion of those matters -- about those matters, because the heads of the municipal HVOs were in contravention of the regulations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... was not in full control, Mr. Boban was not in full control. This has not been translated or recorded. Can we infer from that that Mr. Boban did not fully control these municipalities and he did not want to be faced with problems with these people? If I have understood you correctly, you had to take out a loan to balance your budget.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I was going to make an intervention back on page 20, line 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You had indicated, sir, that the presidents of the municipalities made use of their position as members of the HZ-HB. They were members? of --

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mate Boban was also a member of the Presidency, was he not, by virtue of his position as president of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And during that time, was he also -- was he still the president of the HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we go on to the next document, we're going to look at Orasje very quickly. This is 1D 01747, just as a way of an example of another municipality. This is a conclusion to initiate activities to establish a local border crossing between the municipalities of Orasje and Zupanja, and this is 14 September 1992. Can you please comment on this very quickly?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality is making due. This is a municipality on the border, the border with Croatia, and it's on the River Sava, but the bridge was destroyed so you can only cross with small boats. There were many small farmers who sold their produce in Zupanja in Croatia, so this is an attempt to establish a local border crossing to enable those farmers to sell their produce in Croatia. But of course it is not within the remit of the municipality to take care of such matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we look at 1D 02540, one more example. This is a conclusion on the adoption of the decision on salaries for members of units. This is 27 November 1992. And perhaps you can help us out here.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal HVO sets the amounts of the salaries for the members of the municipal HVO of Posusje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And was that consistent with what was in place at the time or was this something that the municipalities were entitled to do?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without the Defence Department or, rather, without the approval of the Defence Department, they were not authorised to do it themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Finally, just as an example, let's look at Tuzla again. 1D 00365. This is in January. I believe it's 1993, so there should be a correction on the very first page. This is a decision on the functioning of productive branches of the economy and financial institutions in wartime. And again just an example of how Tuzla is coping with the situation on the ground, if you could look at this document, and of course in addition to whatever comments you want to make, if you could also comment on Article 9 and Article 15.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality, with this decision, takes over some authority from the republic and regulates the functioning of businesses and financial institutions in wartime, similar to what the HZ-HB did, only companies that had their corporate headquarters outside of the Tuzla municipality had to register themselves temporarily in that municipality. That's Article 7. And Article 8 says that parts of the enterprises that functioned in that area, but did not have a legal personality, these are provided for by Article 8. And then there is mention of the process of privatization, the transformation of property, which is stopped by this decision. And Article 15 practically puts a ban on trade for private companies, and trade is only allowed for companies the founder of which is the Tuzla municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And can you comment globally? What Tuzla is doing, is that consistent with Republican laws under the circumstances? The measures that Tuzla is taking, are they necessary and appropriate, in your opinion, just very briefly?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my mind, those measures were necessary and appropriate, and the municipality adopts these measures because the existing institutions do not -- were not functioning and were not passing regulations. But the situation in Tuzla was different from the situation elsewhere, so they are -- they are crafting solutions they think are best for themselves. It was similar in other -- at other places, and Sarajevo was practically the only place that reacted in accordance with the regulations of the republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, because that was basically the only area that was under direct control of the Sarajevo government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. We're going to move on to another topic very quickly, and in fact I have very little left in my direct examination. So we could move very quickly to the next set of documents, and this deals with Dr. Jadranko Prlic. I'm going to have you look at document 1D 01596, 1597, 1598, 1599, and 1600. We've seen these documents before. We even heard testimony about these documents before, but if you could just look at it very briefly. And let me ask you, if we look at the very first document, 1D 01596, we see that it's dated May 21, 1993, that Dr. Jadranko Prlic is appointed or is acting as president of the transitional government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Were you aware of this, and could you please comment very briefly on that?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with that period. In that period, Mr. Prlic practically started acting as the prime minister of that transitional government, as can be seen from the numbers used. The purpose was to establish a government as soon as possible and to transit to a more peaceful way of life in Bosnia-Herzegovina, at least in the area of HZ-HB. That is why the Croatian side wanted to get going immediately, and Mr. Prlic took these steps. At the time, he didn't even exert his duties as the president of the HVO HZ-HB, but he immediately started working in this position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'd like to stick with this first document just for a second, and we can see this with the other documents as well that I just named off, but at the very top we see: "Mostar, May 21, 1993," and then we see "Number 1-JP/93." Now, I take it you were familiar with how the numbering system went at the time. Can you please decipher that for us, because if we look at the following document, we see number 4, then we see a number 5, a number 6. Could you please describe that, you know, explain that to us, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the simplest way of marking documents. It shows that as of May 21st, Mr. Prlic started acting as a prime minister or president of the government, but without a real office and real staff, and an official nomenclature, as we call it, but Mr. Prlic started exerting his duties, but he used this system of marking with a serial number, his initials and the year on each document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if we look at the bottom of the page, we see his name. Do you recognise that signature, and can you confirm to us whether indeed that is Dr. Jadranko Prlic's signature in this document as well as the other documents, that is, 1597, 1598, 1599?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Unless there are any questions from the Bench, I will go on to my next and last topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. I have a question, Witness, for you. Mr. Karnavas has shown us a series of documents that contain numbers such as 1456. I would be interested in number 2. We don't seem to have a number 2. At the time, did you know that Mr. Prlic was prime minister of a government in transition? Had he told you that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was familiar with that. That was after the talks in Medjugorje, and then he initiated this activity. I personally, in that period, was still head of the Finance Department of the HVO HZ-HB and did not take part in the implementation of the Medjugorje agreement. But I knew that Mr. Prlic was elected president. He had informed us of that, and he launched subsequent activities. But I was not familiar with the content of documents 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the creation of this transitional covenant is concerned, did you take part in this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That depended on the attribution of positions. I was interested in continuing the activities in building Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Transitional cabinet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see that Mr. Izetbegovic answers Mr. Prlic. This is document ID 1600. We have Mr. Izetbegovic's reply in this document. Had you been made aware of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have held high-ranking positions on the political stage, and you were involved in the administration of this community. Do you feel that this kind of response, in political terms, is something which resembles an acknowledgment of this government in transition, because in Medjugorje they say that his role as prime minister had been vetted and that there would be consultations to appoint other people to other positions? Is this a form of acknowledgment of Mr. Izetbegovic of Mr. Prlic as at the head of this government in transition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it as such, but here we see a process of stalling and at the same time speeding up the activities on setting up the government, because we expected this process to go much faster. But here a proposal is made that lower levels of government be dealt with first, but it is clear that one could not get a solution before such issues were resolved first at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina, because the defence was a key issue and so was financing, and this could not be solved at the level of provinces, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was this process not controlled at two levels, i.e., the regional SDAs, where he says that he had given instructions, but there was the other control which was at the military level? This seems to be what this letter states in its conclusions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are the elements that are used as a pretext for the extension of deadlines for those activities. Now information is collected about potential candidates at the regional SDA boards, and then as the next step we have that first of all it would all depend on military activities, in other words, for as long as there are military operations it would be difficult for us to get those names. And all of this indicates this was just stalling tactics to make sure that the provisional government is set up as late as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you believe that the Muslim side was slowing the process down? Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, the next topic is the Washington Agreement, post-Washington Agreement. As I understand it, you were, as we heard already, you were involved in the process of implementing the Washington Agreement. If I may point out for the record, Your Honours, that the gentleman's answer to your question on line 6 is not recorded. So if I could go back. You were asked, Mr. Tomic, by President Antonneti: "So you believe that the process was slowing the process down." What is your answer to that?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want to make sure that I've nailed this point. Do you believe, in looking at what Izetbegovic is saying, that Mr. Izetbegovic was genuinely acting as a partner in peace?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I was not aware that you were about to answer, and I will have a question after it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on this experience and the procedure to establish the Federation, we could see a lot of elements that indicated that the Bosniak side was not really interested in the establishment of this form of government and that it constantly saw all the agreements as stages leading to this final goal, which was the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina based on the principles that they advocated, and the establishment of any other forms was something that they tried to stall, because those were contrary to the concept of Bosnia and Herzegovina that was part of their political platform. You could see that from the process of the establishment of federal authorities and the functioning particularly in the period when there was this joint government of the Federation and the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could just get one follow-up question before your question, Judge Trechsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say "their principles, their concept," to your understanding what was their concept? And we're speaking about the SDA leadership, in particular Izetbegovic and his cohorts.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the principle of a centralised state based on the "one man, one vote" principle. And in Bosnia and Herzegovina, it was not tenable, it could not function.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, you have said, in answering Judge Antonetti on page 15, line 9, that the letter of Mr. Izetbegovic and the efforts to slow down the process were a pretext, a pretext for the extension of the deadlines. I wonder what you meant by "pretext." What were they hiding, and was there any norm, any legal obligation for them to act otherwise than they did, than Izetbegovic did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the period where direct. political and, I'd say, administrative government in the area controlled by the BH Army was concentrated in the hands of Mr. Izetbegovic, and he was able to start the process of setting up the transitional government by appointing the candidates and following this procedure much more quickly. At the time, it was very important for this transitional government to start functioning with the people who represented the whole area that was controlled by the BH Army and by the HVO HZ-HB, because at that time we mostly had people from Sarajevo in government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think I will not pursue this further now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We can take the break now or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, yes, it's time to have a break now. We shall have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, I think you're beyond seven hours already. I think you must have used seven hours and ten minutes, if I'm not mistaken. Six minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'll be finishing up very soon, Mr. President, and I do realise that we have gone a little bit over time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In light of the questions that were asked earlier, I want to go back to the last chapter that we were, and I want to focus your attention to 1D 01596, because the question was whether Izetbegovic had an obligation. And we see here that the letter sent by Dr. Jadranko Prlic, this is his first letter or number 1, May 21, in the very first paragraph says: "Pursuant to the agreement reached in Medjugorje on May 18, 1993, regarding the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan in Bosnia-Herzegovina ..." Now, do you know whether this agreement in Medjugorje also included internationals in cobbling up this agreement or was this simply an agreement between Izetbegovic, Boban and others?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: International peace mediators were also present there. They insisted that the agreement should be implemented as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've been in government, you've served in various ministries. Do you think that the president of a Presidency of a country such as Bosnia-Herzegovina, albeit during a war period, when he undertakes to sign an agreement with international counterparts that include both the United Nations and the European Union, that the president of the Presidency should comply with the agreements and abide by the agreements, or is it something just to be considered?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be logical for this agreement to be honoured, complied with, and this is how we looked at it. We saw it as an agreement that obliged us to act.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we look at -- to 1D 01599, that's the second-to-last document in this packet, we see this is dated -- actually, I don't have -- yeah, dated 23 May, is directed to Dr. Haris Silajdzic, who was then apparently the Minister of Foreign Affairs. Did you know Mr. Silajdzic?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know of his position at the time?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the foreign minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if we see that -- in the first paragraph, it says that: "In accordance with the agreement," that is, of May 18th, 1993 - we can see that from the very first line making reference to the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan - "Dr. Jadranko Prlic is elected as president of the government and you," that is, Silajdzic, "as Minister of Of Foreign Affairs." And then I'll skip back -- down to the very last sentence where it says, or second-to-last: "The governments of the United States of America, France, the Federal Republic of Germany, the European community should also be informed that the ambassador of Croatian nationality will be appointed soon." Now, looking at this, can you please give us an opinion as to whether Dr. Prlic is seriously trying to implement the agreement that was reached and signed by those who are at Medjugorje, including, that is, Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was a serious intention, because the objective was to take part in the government and to build Bosnia and Herzegovina on different kind of relations and to do it as soon as possible, and to provide the correct information to the International Community in context with their representatives, and that is why the position of ambassador was one of the priority posts, because Mr. Silajdzic, as the Minister of Foreign Affairs at the time, would always present just the views of the authorities in Sarajevo, the views of the Muslim leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and by the way, Your Honours, the agreement is 1D 02404, should you wish to look at it or make reference to it. But let me go on, because if we look at now 1D 1600, and this is -- your answer to this document sort of provoked a series of questions, and you had indicated that you can see, and I'm paraphrasing, that essentially Izetbegovic is dragging his feet, as it were. In other words, he's really not committed to this agreement and is stalling. In order to look at this, you have to look -- let's go back to the very first document, 1D 01596. We can see it's dated May 21, 1993, and when we look at 1D 01600, we see that Izetbegovic is making reference to the May 21 letter from Mr. Prlic, so obviously we know that the letter went out, was received, and this was the response, or at least a reasonable conclusion can be drawn based on this circumstantial evidence. If we then go on and look at the second paragraph in Dr. Jadranko Prlic's letter, we see that he's requesting for Mr. Izetbegovic to designate the sectors in the government, the ministers that the SDA or the Muslims would want in this newly-formed government, based on the agreement reached in Medjugorje on May 18, 1993, pursuant to the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan. Now, looking at paragraph 2 of Izetbegovic's letter, 1D 01600, we then see Izetbegovic saying that in order for him to propose the candidates, it is necessary for him, as the president of the SDA as well as the president of the Presidency, to know which portfolios would be available, although he does designate an interest, but then does not designate any particular names that he -- of candidates that he may have in mind. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then we see -- and I take it -- and this is where I want you to comment on, because here, aside from not providing any names, Mr. Izetbegovic says: "I also think that right now, taking into consideration the circumstances," and who knows what he's talking about at this point, what circumstances, "it is more urgent to start with the establishment of the provisional governments in Mostar, Travnik and Zenica, and it is simpler since those governments do not exist yet. Of course, the activities related to forming a provisional government and central government can run parallel with that." And then he indicates that he has requested the regional committees of the SDA to prepare a candidates list. If you could spend a couple of seconds on this, and tell us, why is it that you think that, based on paragraph 3, it appears that Izetbegovic is stalling and is not genuinely interested in implementing the agreement that he just signed off on? And we're talking only a matter of a few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I'm going to object to that question to the extent that it calls for speculation. If Mr. Tomic can point to any sort of objective, real-world factors that he was aware of at the time, but for him to second guess what was or was not in Mr. Izetbegovic's mind, to that extent the Prosecution objects to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You had indicated, prior to the question that was posed by Judge Trechsel, you had indicated that one would start at the top and move their way down, as opposed to starting at the regional level and moving their way up. Could you please explain to us why you gave that answer, on what basis, you having, of course, the experience of various positions in government?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, the goal is to set up provincial governments in Travnik, Mostar and Zenica, as proposed by Mr. Izetbegovic, because he says they do not exist. But other provincial governments that were supposed to be established under this agreement did not exist at the time either, so practically this was an attempt to abolish the HZ-HB that existed in this area, but the issue of financing the HVO, financing the defence and all the other issues, those issues were not solved, and they could not be solved at the provincial level. Those could only be solved at the level of the state, and this is why it is logical to first set up the state framework, to define all that, and then to go down to the provincial governments to channel funds and to define rights and obligations and so on and so forth. So by stressing the provincial level, in essence, they wanted to abolish the HZ-HB without providing a solution setting up the government in Sarajevo in accordance with the Medjugorje agreement before doing that. And this process cannot go in parallel to the other, because it would engender chaos in terms of financing, of the enforcement of regulations, legislation, and all the other consequences that follow from abolishing a set of administrative and other mechanisms and establishing new ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tomic, you had indicated that it was your impression, having participated in the implementation of the Washington Agreement, which I suspect, since that was signed and agreed upon, the Muslim government was genuinely interested in implementing, that it was your impression that even there they were not interested in truly establishing the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Could you please explain to us how is it that you came up with this impression?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Washington Agreement and the Constitution of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, it is clearly stated that until the federal institutions are established, new institutions, in other words, the provisional administrative arrangements would continue to exist, as defined in the Washington Constitution. That was the definition of the HZ-HB. That meant that new institutions had to be created. But when we arrived in Sarajevo, we were offered to merely include those institutions into the existing institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was contrary to the provisions of the agreement, and this delayed the implementation of the Washington Agreement. So instead of setting up the customs administration of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as envisaged by the agreement, we were told that we should simply agree that the customs areas in the HZ-HB would become areas that would be part of the Customs Administration of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Constitution also envisaged that the Federal Central Bank would be established. Of course, they didn't even want to talk about it because the National Bank of Bosnia-Herzegovina existed, so why shouldn't we accept that? And underlying all that was an effort to delay things, to stall until it would be possible to set up Bosnia and Herzegovina. And there were such examples in all institutions that had to be set up at the level of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Hopefully you are piquing the interest of some of us in this courtroom with your answer. If you could tell us -- if you could please tell us whether -- before I go on to my next question, on page 24, line 8 -- on page 37, line 8, if you could -- and then if you could just sort of slow down a little bit, are we talking about the central -- you said "central bank of Federation," so was it envisaged that the Federation would have a central bank in addition to there being a central bank for Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Washington Agreement stipulated that there should be a federal central bank, the central bank of the Federation, the Muslim-Croat Federation as it was styled at the time, but that area, the area of Federation after the Washington Agreement, was the area where the National Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina could operate, because this institution had no jurisdiction over the Serbian republic, and then the Bosniak side insisted that we should not set up the federal central bank, but to accept the National Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina in its stead. At that time, of course we did not know what the situation was with this bank, what kind of credits and debts it had incurred, and we could not agree to it at all. It was impossible. And that is why in the Washington Agreement it was envisaged that the federal central bank would be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me just put it very bluntly, to cut to the chase on this. It is being alleged in this trial that the Croats and not the Muslims were not interested in the Federation or the implementation of the Washington Agreement, and in fact did everything they possibly could to undermine it, and that continued on with the Dayton Accords. So I'm going to ask you concretely: In your opinion, did you and the other Croats from Bosnia-Herzegovina who were engaged in the implementation of the Washington Agreement, try to impede, frustrate, the implementation of the Washington Agreement?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who take -- who took part in the activities of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina exclusively tried to implement the Washington Agreement the way it was written. That applies to the other documents that are a part of that Washington Agreement. The problem was, as I said, the approach. The Bosniak side did not accept that as the establishment of new government institutions, but as the return of the Croats to the institutions, which was not defined as such in the Washington Agreement. There were constant efforts for those institutions that had been established to be considered the only legal institutions, and the institutions in existence in HZ-HB should be included or become part of the old institutions of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The following reasoning was given: that the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina is a legal successor, so the argument of the continuity of government, which applies to the Republic and the Federation. When we saw that we could not impose the solutions envisaged by the Washington Agreement, we tried the government of the Federation -- for the government of the Federation to become a separate entity from the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This took a while, but then there were meetings of the government of the Federation and after ten minutes there would be a session of the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the composition of both was the same. But there was -- there were no clear provisions as to what the government of the Federation was supposed to do and the government of the Republic respectively, but because the existing structures had some prerogatives, that was not in line with the old Constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the Muslim side insisted that their institutions were older and that they were the only ones that we should -- be included in the structure of those institutions. And they did not accept the guarantees of the National Bank of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down. The interpreters can't follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Slow down a little bit. They didn't catch the last part of your answer, so you may have to repeat that, where you say "they did not accept the guarantees of the National Bank." Could you complete that thought? And I have to go back and correct another line.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So then the efforts to establish a financial system of the Federation, it was necessary for bank guarantees in the Federation are accepted in, say -- for the purposes of customs, but the National Bank of Bosnia-Herzegovina was not willing to accept guarantees of the Hrvatskabanka Mostar, although that bank received actually the approval for work from the National Bank in 1992. They argued that the only legal banks are those in areas under the control of the Army of BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, going back to page 39, line 10 and 11, you said those who participated in the government of BiH were trying to implement the agreement, the Washington Agreement, as it was written. I'm paraphrasing, of course, but who was trying to implement the agreement, the Washington Agreement, as it was written; the Croat side, the Muslim side, or both sides?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking about the establishment of the federal government institutions, the Croatian side had the -- had priority and the initiative in the implementation of the Washington Agreement. The Croatian ministers authored about 80 per cent of the new regulations that we proposed as regulations of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please describe to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas. You asked a very precise question, and it was not answered. The question was: Which side wanted to implement to the letter? That's the way your words were translated, "to the letter." And the way it is translated, one reads that it was the Bosnia and Herzegovina side, but it can mean a lot of things. Perhaps you can explain what you meant by saying that they, whether it is a misprint and then what it means when they say they want to implement to the letter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Croatian side wanted to implement the Washington Agreement literally, to the letter. That is a bid, new institutions. The customs administration of the Federation, the central bank of the Federation, the tax administration of the Federation, the financial police of the Federation, the SDK of the Federation, the way it is stated in the Washington Agreement, and where it also said exactly that until the establishment of new federal institutions, the existing institutions should continue functioning, so including the institutions of HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And while I have, anyway, interrupted, could you please tell the Chamber what time frame you're talking about? When was all this going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the period after the Washington Agreement, 1994 and the beginning of 1995, until the signing of the agreement on the implementation of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I understand it from your previous testimony, during this period you were serving both as Minister of Finance for Bosnia-Herzegovina and Minister of Finance for the Federation.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you know what position, if any, Dr. Jadranko Prlic held at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was Minister of Defence and a vice-president of government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Minister of Defence for Bosnia-Herzegovina or for the Federation, or for both?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Both. [Interpretation] For both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And vice-president of government. Which government, the Federation or BiH, or both?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could just briefly tell us, who were some of the other Croats who were engaged at a high level, such as yourself and others, as Dr. Prlic, that is, who were other Croats that were engaged in this process that had ministerial positions?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Mr. Zubak and Mr. Tadic. There was Mr. Ljubic. Those were all people who had positions in the HZ-HB. And when the Washington Agreement was signed, they went to Sarajevo to implement that agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Zubak, Kresimir Zubak, what position did he hold, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while, he was the president of the Federation with Mr. Ganic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And Mr. Tadic, we're talking about Mato Tadic?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mato Tadic was Minister of Justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what about Mr. Ljubic, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ljubic was minister or vice-minister. At the time when a Croat was minister, his deputy was a Muslim, a Bosniak, and Mr. Ljubic was the president of the Constitutional Assembly. I'm speaking of Mr. Mariofil Ljubic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now, did there ever come a time -- you indicated that it seemed that the Muslim side, the SDA side, the Izetbegovic side, was not really interested in implementing the Washington Agreement, at least as it was envisaged by those who had signed on to it. As a result of that, did the Croats ever complain, and if so, how and to whom?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To government sessions, cabinet sessions, we were trying to solve that issue, but without success. Also, we informed Mr. Tudjman, the president of Croatia, of that, because he was one of the -- one of the persons who signed that agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, why -- you said that he was one of the persons. Did the Washington Agreement envisage some sort of a role for the Republic of Croatia with either the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina or the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Washington Agreement had some other provisions apart from the -- apart from the Constitution. There was the agreement of the Confederation and the access to the port of Ploce and free passage through the Neum belt, and thus the role of the Republic of Croatia was present in the implementation of the Washington Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But why go to Croatia and to President Tudjman? Why not go to Bill Clinton or Holbrooke or Redman? I believe it was Redman who was the one that took the lead for the US State Department. Why not go to those individuals and complain that the Muslims were not complying with the Washington Agreement?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must stress that we also contacted representatives of the International Community. I personally, from the moment on when we established contact with the World Bank and the IMF, I asked them that before meetings, they should require the persons on the Bosnia-Herzegovinian side to produce an accreditation to clearly state who they're representing, the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Republic of Herzegovina, et cetera. So we did contact international representatives, that is, all those who were involved in the process of the implementation of the Washington Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me just -- because again I've got to go back a little bit. You indicate that you wanted the accreditation to clearly state whether they were representing the state or the federation, and I take it because, like yourself, perhaps, many of the ministers were wearing two hats at the same time.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, but the Bosniak ministers acted primarily as ministers of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the Croatian ones wanted to be seen as federal ministers, that is, as representing the new institutions that had yet to be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, just one -- I just want to make sure that I'm absolutely clear on this, because there may be an issue as to whether you're being consistent. When we talked about the Medjugorje agreement, you indicated that you had to stop -- start at the top, that is, before going to the regional level, which is why Jadranko Prlic was asking for the ministers, and you would establish first the state, then the regional. But now we have this Washington Agreement. Would that principle also not apply, albeit we do have an agreement, but would that principle also apply here, which may account for why the Muslims were behaving the way they were; that is, you first have to strengthen or get the state institutions in order before you can put in place the federation institutions? Is this some kind of a contradiction in your answers or can you at least reconcile the two answers that you have given us? I don't know if I was articulate enough.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation after the Washington Agreement and the existence of the Republic and the Federation in the same area, namely, areas controlled by the Army of BiH and the HVO, and these should be run by the federal government. But at the same time there were the regulations of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the same area, and it was still unclear what the final outcome would be. So on the Muslim side thought that we should implement the regulations of the Republic that would simply be -- also become federal regulations, so we needn't establish a new customs administration, but simply take over the existing Customs Administration of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which would then have two names, the Administration of the Republic and that of the Federation. And that was in contravention of the Washington Agreement and, in fact, an obstruction in the establishment of federal institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to the documents now, because I have to end pretty quickly. Let's go to 1D 01953, 1D 01953. We see these are notes, and we see there's a date, "23 April 1994," and we see your name, as well Dr. Prlic's, and we also see Zulfo Robovic. We saw his name earlier on some of the payroll sheets. We also see Ilija Kozul, who's come here and testified. Could you please explain to us, what are these notes?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the meeting in Mostar when the -- when Mr. Bukovic [phoen] came, the vice-prime minister of the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we discussed the first steps in the implementation of the Washington Agreement. We discussed a number of issues, including financial ones, such as making sure that tax, duties -- tax and contributions are levied and to combat evasion on the part of the final users. The Minister of Finance, Mr. Sead Kreso --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Slow down.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was agreed that the Minister of Finance, Mr. Kreso, would hold a separate meeting to discuss the possibilities for the cooperation between the institutions of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and those of the HZ-HB in the area of finance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was that meeting held?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting was held on April the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where does this document come from, incidentally? I mean, just so we know. We see that it's notes from a meeting, but do you recall who may have taken these notes?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These notes were made in the -- in the HVO HZ-HB, where the meeting was held -- the meetings were held.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, having read these notes, can you tell us whether the contents contained in these notes comport with your memory as to what took place during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's go on to the next document, 1D 01954, and this is dated 12 April 1994. These are excerpts from the area of finance. We see your name at the end of this document, along with Sead Kreso. That was the same individual we spoke of. Can you please explain to us what this document is, this protocol?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the basic agreement between Minister Kreso. I was then deputy minister. Mr. Martinovic, the minister, was absent, about issues pertaining to the establishment of a single tax system in the Federation, and then about the ways of controlling the movement of goods, about the combatting of contraband, about the detection of false humanitarian aid, and then the revenues in the Federation should have the end user clearly designated. Under the agreement, there were the army of BiH and the HVO and all other users until the establishment of federal institutions, which meant at the moment -- at that moment that the budget of the HZ-HB had about 130.000 users or beneficiaries; soldiers, police officers, judges, nurses, pensioners, which means budget beneficiaries, about 130.000. Until the establishment of federal institutions, this funding had to continue, and we had to prevent merchants from making -- from making use of that vacuum, and report to one or the other institution in the Federation. We had a technical meeting and defined that in the first stage we must split up the revenues into those belonging to the budget of HZ-HB and those belonging to the budget of the Republic of BiH in order to avoid conflict about who was entitled to which revenue, which means that we determined that if goods go to Zenica, they must clear customs there, and tax duties should be paid there rather than in Mostar or Siroki Brijeg, and the other way around. If goods are going to Vitez, they must be cleared through customs there and not in Zenica, because we had to make sure that the existing institutions within the Federation are financed. Unfortunately, upon returning to Sarajevo and when that protocol was published, Minister Kreso was fiercely attacked by a part of the Muslim leadership, because he was accused that he had recognised Herceg-Bosna, and this agreement was not fully implemented before early 1995. All activities had -- were stopped, the activities that were to follow and had been agreed - namely, the directors of tax administrations should meet and find solutions to some technical questions. The same applies to the directors of tax administrations, of finance police forces - and come up with ways and means for the functioning of all these services until the establishment of institutions in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And just a correction on page 48, line 25. It should say not "were implemented" but "until early 1995, they weren't implemented."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. This actually relates back to the previous document, and I didn't want to interrupt the witness, but I didn't anticipate that this last answer would be so long. The witness never answered the question that Mr. Karnavas did ask him, and I give Mr. Karnavas full credit for that, but he said were these minutes, these minutes reflected in the last document, where they were taken at the HVO HZ-HB, but he never answered Mr. Karnavas' question as to whose notes they were. I would like to have an answer to that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know who took those notes, sir? The previous document, do you recognise the handwriting, do you know who actually took the notes?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Notes were taken by the HVO secretary, and those are comments made by Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But I think, if I could, because the next question is going to be: Who was the secretary that actually took the notes, if I know my colleague, because I would be asking the same question. Do you know who the secretary was at the time, at least?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at that time, it was Mr. Dzidic. He did this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And forgive me here for a second. If I could go back, because I see that in the original, there are some handwritten notes that are on this document, all right, that are not typed. If we all look at the original of 1D 01953, do you recognise that handwriting and do you know who took those notes?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Mr. Prlic's handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it you can read those scribbles. If you can just answer my question. Can you read what is on there or is this -- I know that I can hardly read my writing.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, parts of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And going back to the question that was posed by Mr. Scott, do you recall who the secretary was that would have prepared these notes to which we now see superimposed some handwritten notes by Dr. Prlic in Croatian?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Miroslav Dzidic took notes. He was the secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That would -- unless there are any -- I think that that's a point of clarification that actually was necessary for the record, and we thank our colleague for bringing it to our attention. All right. If we can go to the next document, 1D 03046. If you could please tell us what this represents, this current fiscal system. We see two columns, "RBiH" and "HZ-HB," so the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. So could you look at this and please tell us where did this come from, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document that was created in the Ministry of Finance of the Republic/Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina after I and my colleague, my deputy, made an analysis of the sector in the sphere of finance, in the areas that we provisionally called as areas controlled by the BH Army and areas controlled by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If I could ask you who your colleague, your deputy, was, and of course if you could tell us, if you know, where he was from.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My deputy was Mr. -- Dr., in fact, Ismuddin Kazetovic. Up until that time, he had been in Tuzla, in the finance office. He dealt with finances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, which possess, I guess, another question, because it came up yesterday. There was an objection raised as to whether you were able to provide information concerning activities that were ongoing during 1992 and 1993 in Tuzla, in the Tuzla municipality. So my question is: While he was your deputy and you were collaborating on the implementation of the Washington Agreement, did you have an opportunity to discuss with Dr. Kazetovic what had been going on in Tuzla and what measures, if any, they had taken during the relevant period of time, that is, 1992/1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kazetovic was an expert, and we mostly talked about the situation in both areas, the options, the solutions that were used to deal with the lack of regulations in this area and lack of institutions. And this is part of a document where we put the results of those analyses into a table, comparing the solutions that were implemented in the areas controlled by the BH Army and areas that were controlled by the HVO in various sectors of the finance sphere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You told us that it was your impression, based on the conduct of your colleagues in Sarajevo, that there was a lack of intestinal fortitude, if I could put it this way, to implement the Washington Agreement to its fullest, that is, in establishing the Federation. Can you tell us whether other municipalities within the Federation found -- or how did they find the conduct by the Sarajevo establishment, political establishment, in the implementation of the Federation?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it differed from one area to another. Let me give you an example, Tuzla. Tuzla was the first to establish the canton/county in accordance with the Washington Constitution, and started to exercise its authority in accordance with the Washington Agreement.
